question: Which model family should be recommended as the default for a churn-prediction notebook?

claims.statement: On a synthetic churn dataset (n=5000, 13.5% positive rate, 5-fold stratified CV), logistic_regression achieved the best selection-rule score (mean ROC-AUC 0.776, std 0.013, rank_score 0.773), ahead of hist_gradient_boosting (0.730), lightgbm (0.728), extra_trees (0.712), and xgboost (0.711).
limitations: Synthetic data built for this demo, not real customer records.
The true churn signal was constructed as a mostly-linear/logistic combination of features, which structurally favors a linear model.

claims.statement: This directly contradicts the registry-wide tendency for LightGBM to have the best mean rank across 11 datasets (DCLAB rule set) — concrete confirmation of DCLAB-R13: there is no universal best model, and an aggregate-evidence default can lose outright on a specific dataset.

A notebook copilot should never hardcode a 'recommended model' badge from registry aggregates alone — it must run the same 5-family screen on the user's actual data and show the real result, falling back to the aggregate only as a prior before real numbers exist.

evidence.selection_rule: Rank by mean ROC-AUC minus 0.25×fold standard deviation, then runtime; training CV only.
